answer: Each Opal-protocol agent identity must solve a Tundra-class memory-hard compute puzzle whose difficulty grows quadratically with the count of identities minted by the same Lotus vouching key: identity N costs roughly N² GPU-seconds. Attestation quorums of 5 peers verify proof-of-work, so faking 10 agents forces ~100× the compute of one, making Sybil sweeps economically unattractive.
